'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**[[Russian military intervention in the Syrian civil war]]
***At least 130 [[Russian Air Force|Russian]] [[airstrike]]s have killed 21 members of the [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant]] in the past 24 hours in the [[Syrian Desert|Badia]] desert, according to the [[Syrian opposition|opposition]] [[Syrian Observatory for Human Rights]]. [https://france24.com/en/live-news/20210220-russian-air-strikes-kill-21-is-jihadists-in-syria-monitor (France 24)]
*[[2021 Myanmar protests]]
**Two people are killed and 40 others are injured in a clash between [[Myanmar Police Force|police]] and demonstrators in [[Mandalay]] as the police fire live ammunition to suppress protesters and force workers back to their jobs. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/02/20/world/asia/myanmar-protesters-killed.html (''The New York Times'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2020–21 North American winter]]
**[[February 13–17, 2021 North American winter storm]], [[2021 Texas power crisis]]
***[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] declares a major disaster in [[Texas]] following a severe winter storm and cold weather that left at least 70 people dead and millions of others without power. The declaration allows federal funds to be spent and made available to affected people. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/president-biden-declares-major-disaster-texas-following-severe-winter-storm-n1258442 (NBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in England]]
*****The [[Secretary of State for Health and Social Care|British Health Secretary]] announces a small step to ease the nation's [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]], allowing care home visitors in [[England]] to be regularly visited by a single friend or family member. This change will take effect on March 8. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-56133291 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary]]
****[[Hungary]] surpasses 400,000 cases of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://hungarytoday.hu/coronavirus-hungary-saturday-new-cases-fatalities/ (Hungary Today)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland]], [[Lineage P.1]]
****[[Ireland|Irish]] health officials say that the three cases of the Brazilian variant of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]] have been contained. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-ireland-brazil-idUSS8N2K900G (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Prime Minister of Russia|Prime Minister]] [[Mikhail Mishustin]] announces the approval of the CoviVac [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] for domestic use in [[Russia]], becoming the third vaccine to be approved despite not yet having undergone any clinical trials. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/02/20/russias-prime-minister-says-country-has-approved-third-covid-vaccine.html (CNBC)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
****Data from the [[Ministry of Health (Israel)|Health Ministry]] show that [[COVID-19 vaccine]]s are 99.2% effective against serious illness, reduce mortality by 95.8% and decrease the chance of hospitalization by 98.9%. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/israel-says-vaccine-dramatically-effective-prevents-98-9-of-covid-deaths/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****The [[Philippines]] reports 239 deaths in the past 24 hours, the second-highest number of daily reported deaths since the beginning of the pandemic, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 12,068. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/philippines-239-new-covid-19-deaths-second-highest-daily-record-14243126 (CNA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan]]
****[[Taiwan]] grants emergency use authorization for the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] vaccine. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/taiwan-grants-emergency-authorisation-for-astrazeneca-covid-19-vaccine (''The Straits Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kuwait]], [[travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[Kuwait]] bans entry to all non-Kuwaiti citizens until "further notice", while its citizens returning from abroad must quarantine at a hotel for a week, and then spend a further week in quarantine at home. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-kuwait-avaiation/kuwait-bans-entry-for-non-kuwaiti-citizens-until-further-notice-civil-aviation-authority-idUSKBN2AK0P0?il=0 (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
***[[New Zealand]] begins a vaccination programme against COVID-19, starting with 70 border workers under strict infection prevention measures. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/national/436802/border-workers-receive-first-covid-vaccinations (RNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***The [[United States]] surpasses 28 million cases of COVID-19. [https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2021/02/20/COVID-19-cases-pass-28-million-in-US-deaths-near-500000/1171613837212/ (UPI)]
*[[2020–21 H5N8 outbreak]]
**[[Russia]] reports their first case of human transmission of highly [[pathogenic]] [[H5N8]] [[Avian influenza|bird flu]] in seven workers at a [[poultry farm]] in the southern part of the country. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2021/02/20/russia-reports-first-case-people-infected-bird-flu-world-health/ (''The Daily Telegraph'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Aftermath of the January 6 United States Capitol attack|Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
**The [[United States Department of Justice|Department of Justice]] and the [[Federal Bureau of Investigation|FBI]] announce that they are investigating whether [[Alex Jones]], [[Roger Stone]], and [[Attempts to overturn the 2020 United States presidential election#Stop the Steal|Stop the Steal]] organizer [[Ali Alexander]] played any role in inciting the [[January 6 United States Capitol attack|January 6 riot]] at the [[United States Capitol]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/fbi-alex-jones-roger-stone-capitol-riots-b1805149.html (''The Independent'')]
*[[Mass shootings in the United States]], [[Crime in Louisiana]]
**Three people are killed, including the gunman, and two others are wounded during a shooting at a gun store and indoor shooting range in [[Metairie, Louisiana]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/02/20/us/louisiana-shooting-gun-shop-three-dead/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Protests against the imprisonment of Pablo Hasél]]
**[[Looting]], [[barricade]]s, and [[riot]]s are reported during the fifth consecutive night of protests mainly in [[Barcelona]], [[Spain]], over the imprisonment of rapper [[Pablo Hasél]]. Several protesters break windows at the [[World Heritage Site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]] of [[Palau de la Música Catalana]] and also attempt to storm the [[Bolsa de Barcelona|Stock Exchange of Barcelona]]. [https://www.abc.es/espana/catalunya/abci-tension-calles-y-pedradas-contra-palau-musica-quinta-noche-protestas-barcelona-202102202018_noticia.html (ABC.es)]
*The [[Moscow City Court]] upholds the three-year prison [[sentence (law)|sentence]] against [[opposition to Vladimir Putin in Russia|opposition]] politician and anti-[[corruption in Russia|corruption]] activist [[Alexei Navalny]]. Navalny now faces [[slander]] charges. His defense had previously said that the [[European Court of Human Rights]] had labeled his arrest as "unlawful". [https://www.dw.com/en/russia-alexei-navalnys-sentence-upheld-by-moscow-court/a-56634384 (DW)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2020–2021 Thai protests]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]], [[impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on politics]]
**[[Prime Minister of Thailand|Prime Minister]] [[Prayut Chan-o-cha]] survives a second [[vote of no-confidence]] in the [[House of Representatives (Thailand)|House of Representatives]], accused of mismanagement of the [[Economy of Thailand|economy]], mishandling of the COVID-19 pandemic, [[corruption in Thailand|corruption]], and abuse of [[human rights in Thailand|human rights]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/asia_pacific/thailands-prime-minister-survives-no-confidence-vote/2021/02/19/266150dc-7336-11eb-8651-6d3091eac63f_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[2021 Australian Open]]
**[[Naomi Osaka]] defeats [[Jennifer Brady]] in the final to win the [[2021 Australian Open – Women's Singles|Women's Singles]]. She is the first player to win a fourth [[Grand Slam (tennis)|Grand Slam]] singles title since [[Maria Sharapova]] at the [[2012 French Open]]. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/amp/tennis/56137685 (BBC News)]
